title: Fluorescence-activated microfluidic droplet screening

knownModelSettings.identity: Codex, an agent based on GPT-6 (provided system identity)
knownModelSettings.note: Exact model variant and reasoning settings are not exposed in the fresh agent context; no values inferred.

sourceInspection.method: direct browser image and full-page screenshot
sourceInspection.observation: White space supports copper horizontal state routes, olive input/state marks, and a distinct blue selection lane. Only the route-color allocation transfers; the state-space architecture and stacked dimensions do not.

MAE shows concrete patches, visible versus masked states and representation changes with stable ordering. This supports using a continuous phase changing to discrete droplets, but its photographic patch composition and encoder/decoder modules do not apply.

palette.reason: The figure needs physically continuous material routes on white and an independent control route. This book explicitly allocates color to routes and small marks rather than large container fills.

roles.olive: aqueous inlet and droplets; fill #E7EED8, stroke #698044, accent #577531
roles.copper: oil-filled channel interior and outline; fill #F7E5D5, stroke #B1703D; accent #AF6228 used for small material-direction marks
roles.blue: detection, controller and electrode relationships; fill #DFE8F5, stroke #627FA8, accent #426EAA
roles.neutral: white canvas, dark labels, neutral secondary text; no stage-by-stage hue cycling

palette.redundancy: Material channels have broad fluid interiors; controls use dashed thin arrows. Filled/open droplets and explicit F ≥ θ / F < θ labels carry the class distinction without hue.

design.composition: One continuous device schematic below an offset control lane. A serpentine incubation section and a Y-shaped sorting channel are the main representation, rather than a chain of named boxes.
design.centralRelationship: Each droplet travels along one continuous oil-filled channel through incubation and detection, then its measured fluorescence controls a downstream electrode that selects the outlet.

visualReview.publicationWidthNote: 672 px at 96 dpi corresponds to 177.8 mm; on-screen physical size depends on display scaling.
corrected: Moved the illustrative detected droplet into the visible detection window.
Separated electrode, trigger and outlet labels from control routes.
Moved the flow-focusing callout away from the oil inlet label.
finalObservations: Continuous aqueous inlet narrows at the flow-focusing cross and becomes individually editable droplets in an oil channel.
The material route remains continuous through the serpentine incubation region, optical detection window and sorting Y-junction.
Both outlet conditions are present with correct inequality signs: collected hits F ≥ θ, waste F < θ.
Detector-to-controller-to-electrode direction is visible, and the downstream actuation region is identified.
Filled/open droplet classes and dashed control routes retain their distinctions in grayscale.
No text clipping or remaining label/connector collision observed in the final exported-file render.

limitations: This is a hypothetical methodology schematic. Channel dimensions, flow rates, incubation duration, physical signal values, sample biology and performance are intentionally unspecified.

Material transport is encoded by editable custom channel paths and direction marks. Automated attached-connector checks cover the control graph; material-path topology was checked manually in the saved render.
Native editability is supported by OOXML objects and successful first-party import. No interactive Microsoft PowerPoint edit test was performed.
F, θ and inequalities are editable Unicode text, not Office equation objects.
Screen and grayscale review do not establish calibrated print fidelity or comprehensive color-vision testing.
summaryKo: 연속 미세유체 채널과 별도의 제어 경로로 구성한 편집형 그림을 완성했습니다. 16개 색상 책 중 olive-copper를 의미별로 배정했으며, 177.8 mm 폭과 축소 흑백 보기에서 필수 경로와 문턱값 분류를 확인했습니다. 실제 실험 결과나 성능 수치는 포함하지 않았습니다.
